/-!
# Chvátal's toughness conjecture

A finite simple graph $G$ is *$t$-tough* (Chvátal, 1973), for a real number $t$, if for every
set $S$ of vertices such that $G - S$ has more than one connected component,
$|S| \ge t \cdot \omega(G - S)$, where $\omega(G - S)$ is the number of connected components of
$G - S$. Equivalently, for every integer $k > 1$, $G$ cannot be split into $k$ connected
components by removing fewer than $tk$ vertices. Complete graphs cannot be disconnected by
removing vertices, so they are $t$-tough for every $t$ (by convention they have infinite
toughness).

Chvátal observed that every Hamiltonian graph is $1$-tough and conjectured that, conversely,
there is a threshold $t$ such that every $t$-tough graph is Hamiltonian. His original guess
$t = 2$ was disproved by Bauer, Broersma and Veldman (2000), but the existence of some threshold
remains open and is known as Chvátal's toughness conjecture.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Graph toughness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_toughness)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [V. Chvátal, *Tough graphs and Hamiltonian circuits*,
  Discrete Math. 5 (1973)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0012-365X(73)90138-6)
- [D. Bauer, H. J. Broersma, H. J. Veldman, *Not every 2-tough graph is Hamiltonian*,
  Discrete Appl. Math. 99 (2000)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0166-218X(99)00141-9)
- [D. Bauer, H. Broersma, E. Schmeichel, *Toughness in graphs — a survey*,
  Graphs Combin. 22 (2006)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00373-006-0649-0)
-/
variable {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} {s t : ℝ}

blocks.docstring:
A finite simple graph `G` is `t`-tough (for a real number `t`) if for every set `S` of
vertices such that `G - S` has more than one connected component, `t * ω(G - S) ≤ |S|`, where
`ω(G - S)` is the number of connected components of the graph `G - S` obtained from `G` by
deleting the vertices in `S`. Here `G - S` is the subgraph of `G` induced on the complement
of `S`.

Complete graphs are `t`-tough for every `t`, because no set of vertices disconnects them.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `SimpleGraph.IsKConnected` (FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/Connectivity.lean) — vertex connectivity via `G.induce (Sᶜ)`; same style used, but connectivity does not count components so it cannot express toughness. `SimpleGraph.IsEdgeConnected` in Mathlib is edge-based and also unsuitable.
justification.name: ChvatalsToughnessConjecture.IsTough
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has graph toughness (checked with `rg -i tough` over both). Defined as: for every `S : Finset V` such that `G.induce Sᶜ` (i.e. G − S) has more than one connected component (`1 < Nat.card (...).ConnectedComponent`), `t * ω(G − S) ≤ S.card` (as reals). This is Chvátal's 1973 definition and is equivalent to Wikipedia's 'for every integer k > 1, G cannot be split into k components by removing fewer than tk vertices'. Complete graphs are t-tough for every t automatically (no S disconnects them; proved as `isTough_top`), so the 'convention' needs no special case.

blocks.name: IsTough
blocks.text:
/-- A finite simple graph `G` is `t`-tough (for a real number `t`) if for every set `S` of
vertices such that `G - S` has more than one connected component, `t * ω(G - S) ≤ |S|`, where
`ω(G - S)` is the number of connected components of the graph `G - S` obtained from `G` by
deleting the vertices in `S`. Here `G - S` is the subgraph of `G` induced on the complement
of `S`.

Complete graphs are `t`-tough for every `t`, because no set of vertices disconnects them. -/
def IsTough [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set V, 1 < Nat.card (G.induce Sᶜ).ConnectedComponent →
    t * Nat.card (G.induce Sᶜ).ConnectedComponent ≤ S.ncard

@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem chvatals_toughness_conjecture :
    ∃ t : ℝ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      3 ≤ Fintype.card V → IsTough G t → G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Chvátal's toughness conjecture** (Chvátal, 1973): there is a number $t$ such that every
$t$-tough finite simple graph on at least three vertices is Hamiltonian.

The restriction to at least three vertices excludes the empty graph and the complete graph on
two vertices, which are `t`-tough for every `t` but have no Hamiltonian cycle.
blocks.name: chvatals_toughness_conjecture

theorem IsTough.mono [Finite V] (hG : IsTough G t) (hst : s ≤ t) : IsTough G s :=

  fun S hS => (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hst (Nat.cast_nonneg _)).trans (hG S hS)

@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isTough_top [Finite V] (t : ℝ) : IsTough (⊤ : SimpleGraph V) t := fun S hS => by
  rw [induce_top] at hS
  have := preconnected_top.subsingleton_connectedComponent (V := ↥Sᶜ)
  exact absurd hS (not_lt.2 (Finite.card_le_one_iff_subsingleton.2 this))
blocks.docstring: The complete graph is `t`-tough for every `t`.
blocks.name: isTough_top
blocks.text:
/-- The complete graph is `t`-tough for every `t`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isTough_top [Finite V] (t : ℝ) : IsTough (⊤ : SimpleGraph V) t := fun S hS => by
  rw [induce_top] at hS
  have := preconnected_top.subsingleton_connectedComponent (V := ↥Sᶜ)
  exact absurd hS (not_lt.2 (Finite.card_le_one_iff_subsingleton.2 this))

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isTough_bot_fin_two (ht : 0 < t) : ¬ IsTough (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) t := by
  intro h
  have h2 : 1 < Nat.card
      ((⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).induce (∅ : Set (Fin 2))ᶜ).ConnectedComponent := by
    rw [Finite.one_lt_card_iff_nontrivial]
    refine ⟨connectedComponentMk _ ⟨0, by simp⟩,
      connectedComponentMk _ ⟨1, by simp⟩, ?_⟩
    rw [Ne, ConnectedComponent.eq]
    simp [Subtype.ext_iff]
  have := h ∅ h2
  simp only [Set.ncard_empty, Nat.cast_zero] at this
  exact absurd this (not_le.2 (mul_pos ht (by exact_mod_cast zero_lt_one.trans h2)))
blocks.docstring:
The edgeless graph on two vertices is not `t`-tough for any `t > 0`: removing no vertex
leaves two connected components.

  have h2 : 1 < Nat.card

    rw [Finite.one_lt_card_iff_nontrivial]
    refine ⟨connectedComponentMk _ ⟨0, by simp⟩,
      connectedComponentMk _ ⟨1, by simp⟩, ?_⟩
    rw [Ne, ConnectedComponent.eq]
    simp [Subtype.ext_iff]
  have := h ∅ h2

  exact absurd this (not_le.2 (mul_pos ht (by exact_mod_cast zero_lt_one.trans h2)))

@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isHamiltonian_top_fin_two : ¬ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).IsHamiltonian := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨a, p, hp⟩ := h (by simp)
  have h3 := hp.isCycle.three_le_length
  rw [hp.length_eq] at h3
  simp at h3

claims.decomposer_note: Single existential Prop `∃ t : ℝ, ∀ G finite simple graph, G t-tough → G Hamiltonian` (t quantified outside, over all graphs on all finite vertex types); t-tough (Chvátal 1973) must be defined since neither Mathlib nor the repo has it — for every vertex cut S with G−S disconnected, |S| ≥ t·(number of components of G−S), with complete graphs t-tough for every t by convention — and degenerate cases need care: Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian` treats the 1-vertex graph as Hamiltonian but the 2-vertex complete graph (infinitely tough) as non-Hamiltonian, so the formalization should restrict to graphs with at least 3 vertices (or equivalently exclude K₂) to avoid the conjecture being vacuously false; the article's disproved t = 2 case is history, not a question posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same proposition `∃ t : ℝ, ∀ V [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V), 3 ≤ Fintype.card V → IsTough G t → G.IsHamiltonian` with a bespoke t-tough predicate matching Chvátal 1973 / the article ('for every S with ω(G−S) > 1, |S| ≥ t·ω(G−S)'); I verified each against the source, the boundary cases (S = univ gives 0 components → vacuous; complete graphs vacuously t-tough; t ≤ 0 makes every graph t-tough so cannot witness the existential since e.g. the edgeless graph on 3 vertices is not Hamiltonian; the ≥3-vertex restriction is the standard convention and needed because the empty graph and K₂ are t-tough for all t but not `IsHamiltonian`). The final file uses c02's structure (module docstring with references, theorem statement over `V : Type`, proven API lemmas `isTough_of_nonpos`, `IsTough.mono`, `isTough_top`, and the test `not_isHamiltonian_top_fin_two`), but with the `Set V`/`Set.ncard`/`Nat.card` encoding of `IsTough` used by c01/c05/c08 (matches the repo idiom `G.induce Sᶜ`), an explicit `[Finite V]` on the definition as in c05 (honest: Nat.card/ncard are junk on infinite types; `Finite` is a Prop so no instance issues), `isTough_top` proved via c01/c04's `induce_top` route, and a new proved test `not_isTough_bot_fin_two` showing the definition is not vacuous. c03/c06 were not used because their `Fintype.card` on `ConnectedComponent` resolves through an odd noncomputable instance path (`CategoryTheory.instFinCategoryOfFiniteOfIsThin`); mathematically equivalent but `Nat.card` is cleaner. c01's extra sorry'd textbook theorem and c04's extra `research solved` t = 2 theorem (no `formal_proof` attribute) are outside the decomposition table and were not shipped.

context:
In graph theory, toughness is a measure of the connectivity of a graph.  A graph G is said to be t-tough for a given real number t if, for every integer k > 1, G cannot be split into k different connected components by the removal of fewer than tk vertices. For instance, a graph is 1-tough if the number of components formed by removing a set of vertices is always at most as large as the number of removed vertices. The toughness of a graph is the maximum t for which it is t-tough; this is a finite number for all finite graphs except the complete graphs, which by convention have infinite toughness.
Graph toughness was first introduced by Václav Chvátal (1973). Since then there has been extensive work by other mathematicians on toughness; the recent survey by Bauer, Broersma & Schmeichel (2006) lists 99 theorems and 162 papers on the subject.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The table's single-slot decomposition and its notes (existential over t outside, bespoke t-tough definition, restriction to ≥ 3 vertices) match the source and were followed.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Chvátal's toughness conjecture

A finite simple graph $G$ is *$t$-tough* (Chvátal, 1973), for a real number $t$, if for every
set $S$ of vertices such that $G - S$ has more than one connected component,
$|S| \ge t \cdot \omega(G - S)$, where $\omega(G - S)$ is the number of connected components of
$G - S$. Equivalently, for every integer $k > 1$, $G$ cannot be split into $k$ connected
components by removing fewer than $tk$ vertices. Complete graphs cannot be disconnected by
removing vertices, so they are $t$-tough for every $t$ (by convention they have infinite
toughness).

Chvátal observed that every Hamiltonian graph is $1$-tough and conjectured that, conversely,
there is a threshold $t$ such that every $t$-tough graph is Hamiltonian. His original guess
$t = 2$ was disproved by Bauer, Broersma and Veldman (2000), but the existence of some threshold
remains open and is known as Chvátal's toughness conjecture.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Graph toughness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graph_toughness)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [V. Chvátal, *Tough graphs and Hamiltonian circuits*,
  Discrete Math. 5 (1973)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0012-365X(73)90138-6)
- [D. Bauer, H. J. Broersma, H. J. Veldman, *Not every 2-tough graph is Hamiltonian*,
  Discrete Appl. Math. 99 (2000)](https://doi.org/10.1016/S0166-218X(99)00141-9)
- [D. Bauer, H. Broersma, E. Schmeichel, *Toughness in graphs — a survey*,
  Graphs Combin. 22 (2006)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00373-006-0649-0)
-/

namespace ChvatalsToughnessConjecture

open SimpleGraph

variable {V : Type*} {G : SimpleGraph V} {s t : ℝ}

/-- A finite simple graph `G` is `t`-tough (for a real number `t`) if for every set `S` of
vertices such that `G - S` has more than one connected component, `t * ω(G - S) ≤ |S|`, where
`ω(G - S)` is the number of connected components of the graph `G - S` obtained from `G` by
deleting the vertices in `S`. Here `G - S` is the subgraph of `G` induced on the complement
of `S`.

Complete graphs are `t`-tough for every `t`, because no set of vertices disconnects them. -/
def IsTough [Finite V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set V, 1 < Nat.card (G.induce Sᶜ).ConnectedComponent →
    t * Nat.card (G.induce Sᶜ).ConnectedComponent ≤ S.ncard

/--
**Chvátal's toughness conjecture** (Chvátal, 1973): there is a number $t$ such that every
$t$-tough finite simple graph on at least three vertices is Hamiltonian.

The restriction to at least three vertices excludes the empty graph and the complete graph on
two vertices, which are `t`-tough for every `t` but have no Hamiltonian cycle.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem chvatals_toughness_conjecture :
    ∃ t : ℝ, ∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      3 ≤ Fintype.card V → IsTough G t → G.IsHamiltonian := by
  sorry

/-- Every graph is `t`-tough for every `t ≤ 0`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isTough_of_nonpos [Finite V] (ht : t ≤ 0) : IsTough G t :=
  fun _ _ => (mul_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg ht (Nat.cast_nonneg _)).trans (Nat.cast_nonneg _)

/-- If `G` is `t`-tough then `G` is `s`-tough for every `s ≤ t`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem IsTough.mono [Finite V] (hG : IsTough G t) (hst : s ≤ t) : IsTough G s :=
  fun S hS => (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hst (Nat.cast_nonneg _)).trans (hG S hS)

/-- The complete graph is `t`-tough for every `t`. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isTough_top [Finite V] (t : ℝ) : IsTough (⊤ : SimpleGraph V) t := fun S hS => by
  rw [induce_top] at hS
  have := preconnected_top.subsingleton_connectedComponent (V := ↥Sᶜ)
  exact absurd hS (not_lt.2 (Finite.card_le_one_iff_subsingleton.2 this))

/-- The edgeless graph on two vertices is not `t`-tough for any `t > 0`: removing no vertex
leaves two connected components. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isTough_bot_fin_two (ht : 0 < t) : ¬ IsTough (⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)) t := by
  intro h
  have h2 : 1 < Nat.card
      ((⊥ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).induce (∅ : Set (Fin 2))ᶜ).ConnectedComponent := by
    rw [Finite.one_lt_card_iff_nontrivial]
    refine ⟨connectedComponentMk _ ⟨0, by simp⟩,
      connectedComponentMk _ ⟨1, by simp⟩, ?_⟩
    rw [Ne, ConnectedComponent.eq]
    simp [Subtype.ext_iff]
  have := h ∅ h2
  simp only [Set.ncard_empty, Nat.cast_zero] at this
  exact absurd this (not_le.2 (mul_pos ht (by exact_mod_cast zero_lt_one.trans h2)))

/-- The complete graph on two vertices is `t`-tough for every `t`, but it is not Hamiltonian,
since a cycle in a simple graph has at least three vertices. This is why the conjecture is
restricted to graphs with at least three vertices. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isHamiltonian_top_fin_two : ¬ (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 2)).IsHamiltonian := by
  intro h
  obtain ⟨a, p, hp⟩ := h (by simp)
  have h3 := hp.isCycle.three_le_length
  rw [hp.length_eq] at h3
  simp at h3

end ChvatalsToughnessConjecture

items: Restricted the conjecture to graphs with at least three vertices (`3 ≤ Fintype.card V`). Without it the statement is false for degenerate reasons: the empty graph and K₂ are t-tough for every t (no vertex set disconnects them) but are not `SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian` (a cycle in a simple graph has length ≥ 3). The literature (e.g. Bauer–Broersma–Schmeichel survey) states the conjecture for 't-tough graphs on at least three vertices'. The test lemma `not_isHamiltonian_top_fin_two` documents this.

`t` ranges over all of ℝ, matching 'there is a number t'. Nonpositive t cannot witness the existential (every graph, including disconnected ones, is t-tough for t ≤ 0, see `isTough_of_nonpos`), so no positivity restriction was added.

Vertex types are quantified as `V : Type` (universe 0) inside the existential, following the repo idiom (e.g. ErdosProblems/619.lean, WrittenOnTheWallII files). Finite graphs in higher universes are isomorphic to ones in `Type`, so nothing is lost.

`IsTough` does not itself assume `Fintype V`: the definition uses `Finset V` and `Nat.card` of the connected components, which needs no finiteness or decidability instances. The conjecture supplies `[Fintype V]`, so all uses are finite, where `Nat.card` is the exact component count. Removal of `S` is modeled by `G.induce ((S : Set V)ᶜ)`, the same idiom as the repo's `IsKConnected`.
Used Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian` (existence of a Hamiltonian cycle; 1-vertex convention is irrelevant given the ≥ 3 vertex restriction).
The disproved t = 2 case is recorded in docstrings as history only, per the decomposition notes.

reviewer_notes: Statement source is terse; the definition of t-tough was taken from the Graph toughness article and Chvátal 1973 (all candidates agree). Modeling decisions in the final file: t ranges over ℝ (no positivity hypothesis; nonpositive t cannot witness the existential); graphs are finite simple graphs on arbitrary `V : Type` with `[Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]` (the latter only because Mathlib's `SimpleGraph.IsHamiltonian` requires it); the domain restriction `3 ≤ Fintype.card V` follows the standard Hamiltonicity convention and is required because the empty graph and K₂ are t-tough for every t under the cut definition yet not `IsHamiltonian` in Mathlib — this is explained in the theorem docstring and witnessed by the proved test `not_isHamiltonian_top_fin_two`. The bespoke `IsTough` lives in the problem file (single-file constraint); a maintainer may prefer moving it to `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/Combinatorics/SimpleGraph/` as `SimpleGraph.IsTough` since it is reusable. All non-slot declarations are proved (`category API`/`test`), so the only `sorry` is the conjecture. File compiles under `lake env lean` with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning; the one >100-char line is a reference URL, as is common in FormalConjectures/Wikipedia.

title: Chvátal's toughness conjecture
